quotedShalls.requirement: Branch Activation Is Verified, Compare-and-Swap, and Atomic
quotedShalls.quote: The same transaction SHALL lock and verify the current unexpired lease ID, owner, and epoch while comparing the expected head/generation, then activate the candidate, increment the generation by exactly one, supersede the prior branch, publish artifact invalidations, and enable new-generation effects.
quotedShalls.bearing: Supersession of the prior branch and installation of the replacement head are ONE transaction. A COMMITTED head naming a superseded branch is therefore a state no activation can produce.

quotedShalls.requirement: Branches Preserve Immutable Parent and Base Lineage / Scenario: Authorized rewind creates replacement branch
quotedShalls.quote: the prior branch SHALL remain unchanged and effective until activation succeeds
quotedShalls.bearing: There is no legitimate transient in which the head's branch is non-effective.

quotedShalls.requirement: Branch Resolution Preserves Contiguous Order and Integrity / Scenario: Branch suffix has a gap or digest mismatch
quotedShalls.quote: the branch SHALL be quarantined or blocked with a typed integrity error
quotedShalls.bearing: Typed integrity refusal (and the word 'quarantined') is the spec's established answer to persisted integrity failure.

quotedShalls.requirement: Branch Rollback Preserves the Effective Head and Generation
quotedShalls.quote: command, effect, and correction admission SHALL stop and the stream SHALL expose a typed truthful blocked state
quotedShalls.bearing: A typed truthful blocked state that stops command admission is exactly what the MATCH_QUARANTINED frame implements at the intent boundary.

quotedShalls.requirement: Scenario: Player command targets stale branch
quotedShalls.quote: the server SHALL return `STALE_BRANCH` with the active head and resync action / AND it SHALL append nothing
quotedShalls.bearing: STALE_BRANCH OWES an active head. Under a corrupt head there is no trustworthy active head, so STALE_BRANCH would have to lie. Correctly rejected by the author.

wireConsistency.definition: src/types/multiplayer/Protocol.ts:784-787 — 'Umbrella 15.4 binder: recovery refused this match's authority and quarantined the session. Distinct from UNKNOWN_MATCH so a known corrupt match is not described as missing.'
wireConsistency.assessment: Consistent. The code's stated meaning is 'a KNOWN match whose authority was refused' — precisely this case. The frame contract (Protocol.ts:739-741) says 'Connection stays OPEN unless the server also follows up with `Close`', so an Error frame alone is a non-fatal refusal by definition.

consumerAudit.method: grep MATCH_QUARANTINED across src/ and e2e/; trace the client Error-frame path end to end
consumerAudit.preExistingProducer: src/lib/multiplayer/server/bindMultiplayerSocketConnection.ts:330 via refusalForMissingHost, delivered through closeWithTypedError (:390-407) which sends Error + Close + socket.close(1008). reason = 'match-quarantined'.
consumerAudit.newProducer: ServerMatchHostBranchAdmission.ts:166 and :240 via refuse(), which sends an Error frame ONLY (ctx.broadcast) and does NOT close. reason = 'history-integrity-blocked'.
clientPath: src/lib/multiplayer/client.ts:389-401 — Error handler settles the pending intent by intentId and re-emits { code, reason, conflictHead, recoveryAction }. No code-specific branching, no close, no state deletion.

src/hooks/useMultiplayerSession.helpers.ts:271-296 handleClientError — any string code other than 'CLIENT_ERROR' goes to setProjectionSignal (only if non-null) + setIntentError. It does NOT set status 'error' and does NOT set closedInfo for a coded frame.

src/lib/multiplayer/tacticalLifecycleState.ts:86-100 projectionSignalFromServerError — handles only PROJECTION_REBUILDING and STALE_BRANCH; every other code returns null ('deliberately total and deliberately narrow ... an unknown code must map to "no signal" rather than throw').
consumerAudit.misinterpretationRisk: NONE FOUND. No client-side code branches on MATCH_QUARANTINED at all: zero non-server, non-test references. There is no auto-leave, no local-state delete, no socket teardown driven by the code. Session teardown is driven by the separate Close frame / socket close (createClientCloseHandler), which this path does not emit.

recoveryActionOmission.typeLevel: SAFE — ErrorMessageSchema (Protocol.ts:805-830) declares conflictHead, activeHead and recoveryAction as .optional(), documented 'Optional because most error codes have no head to report'. tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json exit 0 re-run in this review.
recoveryActionOmission.runtime: SAFE — client.ts passes recoveryAction through as undefined; readRecoveryAction is only reached for STALE_BRANCH. The pre-existing MATCH_QUARANTINED producer (bindMultiplayerSocketConnection.ts:330) likewise carries only a reason, so a reason-only quarantine frame is already the shipped shape.
recoveryActionOmission.conflictHeadOmission: Correct and spec-required: naming a head here would invite a resync onto the corrupt row, which the gm-combat 'Player command targets stale branch' scenario forbids by demanding the ACTIVE head.

observations.title: Protocol.ts MATCH_QUARANTINED docstring now under-describes the code
observations.detail: Protocol.ts:784-786 still attributes the code solely to the 'Umbrella 15.4 binder'. The code now has a second, structurally different producer (a live per-intent refusal that does not close the socket). The two are distinguishable only by `reason` ('match-quarantined' vs 'history-integrity-blocked').
observations.recommendation: Add one comment line at Protocol.ts:784 in a FOLLOW-UP, not this PR — the B surface is at 498/500 and the new producer is thoroughly documented in ServerMatchHostBranchAdmission.ts:26-35. Not required: no consumer reads the docstring, and no behavior depends on it.

observations.title: Refusal is broadcast, not unicast
observations.detail: refuse() calls ctx.broadcast(err) (ServerMatchHostBranchAdmission.ts:308), so every socket on the match receives the MATCH_QUARANTINED frame carrying the originating player's intentId. Pre-existing behaviour shared with STALE_BRANCH and GM_ONLY; not introduced by this commit. Benign here — every peer on a corrupt stream is equally blocked.

2_unreachabilityClaim.verdict: CONFIRMED for the port read path; the author's 'BY CONSTRUCTION' phrasing is slightly stronger than the SQLite write path warrants

sqlitePort.evidence: readEffectiveHead LEFT JOINs event_history_effective_heads to event_history_branches on (stream_type, stream_id, branch_id) and at :146-152 throws EventHistoryBranchError('branch-integrity') unless row.status === 'effective'. A caller can therefore NEVER receive a head naming a non-effective branch — it either gets an effective head, null, or the typed refusal. The subsequent readBranch could not have observed a 'superseded' status.

inMemoryPort.evidence: transitionBranchStatus deletes the head row in the same call that moves a branch off effective: `if (current.status === 'effective' && to !== 'effective') { this.heads.delete(streamKey(stream)); }` (:121-123). The corrupt pair is not representable.

activation.finding: SAFE. The entire sequence runs inside one db.transaction(): transitionBranchStatus(prior,'superseded') at :138, transitionBranchStatus(candidate,'effective') at :139, writeSupersession at :140, repointEffectiveHead at :148. The stranded-head window exists only inside the uncommitted, synchronous better-sqlite3 transaction and is never committed. This matches the spec SHALL quoted above.

portApiGap.finding: The SQLite port's transitionBranchStatus (SQLiteEventHistoryBranchStore.ts:233-259) ONLY updates the branch row — unlike the in-memory port, it does NOT drop or repoint the head. A direct caller doing transitionBranchStatus(stream, <effective branch>, 'superseded') outside the activation transaction would therefore COMMIT the corrupt pair through the public port API, with no raw SQL required. This is exactly what the ORIGINAL test did (the pre-repair test called branches().transitionBranchStatus(..., 'root', 'superseded')), so the author's rewrite to raw SQL slightly overstates 'not producible through the API'.
portApiGap.productionExposure: NONE TODAY. Grep of transitionBranchStatus callers outside __tests__ returns only EventHistoryActivation.ts:138-139 plus pure pass-through port wiring (journalCapabilityPorts.ts:231-235, durableCapabilityPorts.ts:69-73, DurableMatchStore.ts:613 declare, JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:308 declare, storeCapabilityPorts.ts:55 interface). No production surface performs a bare supersede.
portApiGap.recommendation: Follow-up (outside this PR and this line cap): make the SQLite port symmetric with the in-memory port — either drop the head row on an effective->non-effective transition, or refuse a bare supersede of the head's branch outside activation. Filing this is the durable fix; it does NOT argue for keeping the removed arm.

armRemovalRecommendation.recommendation: REMOVAL IS CORRECT — do not restore as defense-in-depth.
rationale: The arm is genuinely dead: readEffectiveHead throws before control can reach readBranch, in both ports.

Restoring it would not add defense — it would add a WRONG answer. Its only reachable window was between the two reads, where it would emit conflictHead = the branch the authority has just left, i.e. a resync target that the gm-combat spec scenario explicitly forbids ('STALE_BRANCH with the active head').
Defense-in-depth for this shape already exists and is stronger: the typed branch-integrity refusal at the store, now translated rather than propagated.
The removal is documented in place with the citing comment at ServerMatchHostBranchAdmission.ts:166-175.

predicate.assessment: Both catch sites call `if (!isBranchIntegrityFailure(error)) throw error;` before returning a refusal, so every other EventHistoryBranchError code (unknown-branch, no-effective-branch, invalid-ancestry, duplicate-effective-branch, illegal-status-transition, GENERATION_EXHAUSTED, STALE_CORRECTION_LEASE) and every non-EventHistoryBranchError exception rethrows unchanged. No swallow.

3_errorTranslationScope.catchScope: Each try wraps exactly ONE call — readMatchStreamRebuild (:236-241) and readEffectiveHead (:161-167). getEvents, the servedBranchId comparison, and the refusal construction all sit outside the guards, so no unrelated failure can be absorbed.

noAppendOnRefusal.verdict: CONFIRMED BY TRACE, not only by the test
trace: src/lib/multiplayer/server/ServerMatchHostIntent.ts:215-217 — `const refusal = refuseDuringHistoryRebuild(ctx, envelope) ?? (await refuseLiveBranchFromIntent(...)); if (refusal) return refusal;`

Everything that can write runs strictly AFTER that early return: refuseUnauthorizedCommand (:219), refuseForeignUnitCommand (:235), the rate limiter (:243), duplicate-intent detection (:257+), and the engine/append path below them.
The refusal path itself performs only ctx.broadcast(err) (ServerMatchHostBranchAdmission.ts:308) — a socket send, no store or journal call.
Both reads inside the guards are SELECT-only (SQLiteEventHistoryBranchStore.readEffectiveHead is a single prepared SELECT; readMatchStreamRebuild reads rebuild/head state).
noAppendOnRefusal.testCorroboration: The rewritten test independently pins it at the real SQLite boundary: `expect((await store.getEvents(matchId)).length).toBe(before)` AND `expect(journalCount()).toBe(journalBefore)`, asserted after BOTH the first and the second intent.

4_cutoverTask12Conflict.verdict: REAL BUT NOT A SPEC CONTRADICTION; correctly deferred to the owner — do NOT amend in this PR

text.quote: - [ ] 1.2 S2: route `readEffectiveHead` and the live branch admission consult through the journal head so both `STALE_BRANCH` arms are reachable; prove with the four illegal command shapes the umbrella's 14.2-a receipt names.

analysis: It is a TASK, not a SHALL. No requirement in either delta spec demands two STALE_BRANCH arms; the only STALE_BRANCH SHALL (gm-combat-interventions/spec.md:13) demands ONE behaviour — 'STALE_BRANCH with the active head and resync action' — which the surviving !onLivePath arm delivers. So there is no spec/implementation contradiction today.

The task is UNCHECKED and belongs to a DIFFERENT change (adopt-combat-journal-cutover-and-gm-rewind), whose own rule is that workers never edit openspec/**. Editing it here would also be an out-of-prefix change on a 498/500 budget.

The wording is nonetheless STALE: it predates b1fae82a7's readEffectiveHead join, and an S2 implementer following it literally would resurrect an arm that can only report the branch the authority has just left as the 'active head' — the exact lie the gm-combat scenario forbids.
4_cutoverTask12Conflict.recommendation: Later S2 concern, tracked now. The author's evidence already flags it under decision.flaggedForOwner; carry that flag into the PR description so the S2 owner rules on it before picking 1.2 up. Suggested amended intent for the owner to ratify: 'route readEffectiveHead and the live branch admission consult through the journal head so the STALE_BRANCH arm is reachable on the journal head, and a head not naming an effective branch answers MATCH_QUARANTINED.' No edit required in PR #1674.
